chapter: Gambling, Cab's small groups and Havana
title: Personnel of Cab Calloway's 1946 big band
summary: Hinton and Francis name the sections of Cab's big band when Francis joined in 1946.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And listen. Recently here, we were rehashing some of the experiences in the different bands and we were talking about Lucky's band. Now you joined Cab in '46, was it?
Yeah, 1946.

And I was in that band from '46 to '52, so we spent about, how many? Let's see, '46 to '52 is about six or seven years that we spent together; we were in the big band together. Was Pop Smith in the band with you?
No.
No? He had gone?
Yeah, he had gone when I got there.
He had gone to California when you came in the band.
Yeah, he had just left when I joined the band.
Can you name some of the guys who was in that big band?
Oh, there was Paul Webster, there was Shag Collins, Lamar Wright, Jr.
Was Lamar Wright Senior there?
No, not yet; he hadn't come in yet -- he came in later after I was there.
You mean Lamar Wright Senior came in later, or Junior?
Well, wait a minute now.
Because Lamar Wright Senior was with me.
No, but he was with Lucky and me for awhile, too. He had left the band, left Cab.
Oh, did he?
Yeah. I think he left Cab, because he worked with me Lee in Lucky's band.
Wright, Senior?
Yeah, senior. But when I came in the band, it was Shad Collins, Paul Webster, Lamar Wright, Jr., and I think -- Eddie Mullens.
Oh, I see ... yeah.

Eddie Mullens. Because in the trombone section was Quentin Jackson, Earl Hardy and Kea Johnson. And saxophones were Hilton Jefferson, Sam Taylor, Charlie Frazier, Chops -- Al Gibson. And Gene Michaels.
Yeah, that was a 1946 band.
And John Smith was on the guitar.
Smitty!
And Dave Rivera David Baer played piano, and Milt Bill Hinton -- -- on bass, you Base and myself; that was the band.
